name: crossing_chute_bay1
_why: THE critical passage in this revision. Hopper A is the BACK fill mouth but feeds the FRONT tray, so its chute runs 159mm enclosed -- under tray B, then under hopper B's ramp -- before it opens. This sample line runs parallel to that chute's floor, 15mm above it. If anything ever closes this path, half the bays silently stop feeding and no other check would notice: a sealed passage is still one watertight single-body shell.

name: crossing_chute_bay5
_why: the same passage in the far bay, which is the one the right-hand rail buttress intrudes into

name: outlet_trayA_bay1
_why: tray A's outlet: from inside the tray, under the wall that separates it from tray B, into the chute

name: outlet_trayB_bay5
_why: tray B's outlet: from inside the tray, under hopper B's front wall, into hopper B

name: rail_groove_front
_why: the front joining groove must be open from its floor out of the top of the side wall, or a neighbouring module's rail cannot be lowered in
